thread:
lucia: Heads-up — just handled a new onboarding ticket where the user was blocked for 2 hours because of import/require confusion in the JS SDK docs.

harry: what did they try?

lucia: they had a legacy server using CommonJS and did: `const SDK = require('redwood-inference')` then `new SDK()` -> `TypeError: SDK is not a constructor`.

lucia: they also tried `require('redwood-inference')` in a bundler config and got node polyfills pulled in, big bundle, then runtime errors in Vercel Edge: `ReferenceError: process is not defined`.

patrick: classic mix of (a) default vs named export, and (b) wrong entrypoint for runtime. are we surfacing the `/cjs` and `/edge` entrypoints in quickstart?

docs-eng: currently quickstart only uses ESM examples: `import { Client } from 'redwood-inference'`. Not enough for CJS consumers.

maya: can we add a tiny matrix at top of quickstart: Runtime -> Use this -> Example? saves so many tickets.

lucia: proposed minimal copy for quickstart: 

lucia: "Node (ESM or bundlers): `import { Client } from 'redwood-inference'`
Node (CommonJS / require): `const { Client } = require('redwood-inference/cjs')`
Edge runtimes (Vercel/Cloudflare): `import { Client } from 'redwood-inference/edge'` — ESM only; no `process`/`global` or `fs`."

harry: also call out explicitly: SDK exports named symbols (`Client`, `utils`) — there is no default export. add a one-liner: `Do not use: import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'`.

docs-eng: good. I'll add a short FAQ entry: "Why does require('redwood-inference') throw?" with two bullets: 1) use `/cjs` for require; 2) check Node version and `exports` resolution.

patrick: engineering task: audit package.json `exports` map. ensure conditional exports don't make `require('redwood-inference')` resolve to ESM-only in older Node versions. filing RW-runtime-301.

support-bot: Created issue RW-DX-901: "docs(js): clarify ESM/CJS/edge import examples, export shape, and add smoke tests" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/901 :white_check_mark:

maya: for reproducibility add two tiny smoke checks in sample-apps: `ci/cjs-smoke.js` (runs `node` to require `/cjs`) and `ci/edge-smoke.mjs` (bundles minimal edge import to ensure no node globals). CI should run them on PRs touching SDK packaging or docs.

lucia: let's also include a debugging snippet in docs: `node -e "console.log(require('redwood-inference/cjs'))"` that prints the exported shape so users can see `{ Client: [Function], version: 'x.y.z' }`.

harry: typings note: for ESM: `import type { ClientOptions } from 'redwood-inference'`. For CJS+TS users show JSDoc: `/** @type {import('redwood-inference').ClientOptions} */ const opts = {}`.

docs-eng: I'll PR the quickstart update with the table, FAQ blurb, and the small debugging example. maya/patrick can you add the sample-app tests and runtime audit respectively and link the PR to RW-DX-901?

maya: will do — adding the cjs smoke and a one-line github action that runs `node ci/cjs-smoke.js`.

patrick: started RW-runtime-301 with notes about conditional exports. will post findings.

lucia: once PRs land, let's update the support playbook: triage question "are you using import or require? (ESM vs CJS vs Edge)" That should cut down back-and-forth.

support-bot: PR checklist updated: include both ESM and CJS code snippets for JS SDK docs, and add edge guidance.

lucia: thanks team. small docs + smoke tests should stop these repeated tickets. I'll paste the PR links here when ready :rocket:
